questions.question: What is the job of a refresh token?
options: To be sent with every API call
To get a new short-lived access token without logging in again
To store the user's password
To encrypt the access JWT
questions.explanation: The refresh token is sent only to the refresh endpoint and is swapped for a new access token.

questions.question: Why is a refresh token usually a random string that the server stores, rather than a JWT?
options: Random strings are shorter to type
The server can look it up, rotate it or cancel it at any time
JWTs cannot hold a user name
Spring Security forbids JWTs for this
questions.explanation: A stored value can be deleted on logout or theft. A self-contained JWT cannot be cancelled before it expires.

questions.question: With rotation on, a client refreshes with value A and receives B. It then sends A again. What does the server return?
options: 200 with a new pair
401, and it may cancel the user's other refresh tokens
204 with no body
500 Internal Server Error
questions.explanation: A was already used. Seeing it again signals theft, so the server rejects it and can end the user's sessions.

questions.question: A user logs out, which deletes the refresh token on the server. The access JWT was issued 2 minutes ago with a 15 minute life. Can it still call the API?
options: Yes, until it expires, because the API only checks its signature and expiry
No, deleting the refresh token also cancels the JWT
No, the API returns 500
Only if the user logs in again
questions.explanation: An access JWT is checked without asking the server's store, so it works until it expires. That is why it must be short.

questions.question: A team stores refresh tokens in plain text in their database table. What is the risk?
options: The table becomes too large
If the database leaks, attackers get working sessions
Refresh tokens stop rotating
The access JWT signature fails
questions.explanation: Store a hash, like a password hash. A leaked plain value can be used at once by anyone.
